VBO:0201285.summary: A Labrador–English Springer Spaniel cross found as both a companion and a hunting dog in Britain. Trainer Pippa Mattinson reports friendly, outgoing Springadors in her experience, while stressing that behaviour and mature size vary. The name describes parentage rather than a uniform temperament; littermates can differ in size, and working instincts are not reliably predicted by the cross alone.
VBO:0201285.shortDescription: A Labrador–Springer cross found in British homes and hunting, with variable size, character and working drive.

sources.title: World Customs Organization — Kenya’s Springador Cooper, 2025 photo competition
sources.evidence: Actual complete PDF page34, Kenya Out in the wild, personally read in English and French and whole rendered page viewed. Explicitly identifies Cooper as Labrador–Springer Spaniel mix (Springador), member of Kenya detector team across savannah and borders; team patrol role detects narcotics and explosives. Fourteen is total detector-team count, not Springador count. Own institutional program statement, not population-wide temperament or all-cross working aptitude. Numerical Cooper age/generation/pedigree unknown.

sources.title: Forest Dog Rescue — adult Springador Molly, firsthand foster assessment
sources.evidence: Actual entire substantive page personally read in Chrome and retained HTML/text: Springador, female, age2–3years; lively, intelligent, clever, communicative and affectionate; active exercise and mental stimulation, close company, separation challenges, chase instinct and difficulty with female dogs. Own rescue records failed working assessment and adoption; these are individual facts, no blanket suitability/safety/training prediction. Exact breed label is Springador; ancestry proportions/pedigree not independently established. General parent-breed temperament transfer excluded.

sources.title: Pippa Mattinson / The Labrador Site — The Springador
sources.evidence: Fresh full original article read2026-10-06; updated2025-06-21. Defines Labrador Retriever×English Springer Spaniel, documents British rural pets/hunting companions and author’s firsthand plural Springador observations as friendly/outgoing. Explicitly describes littermate size variation and unpredictable individual trait expression. Copy attributes observations, avoids parent-caused temperament promise, universal energy statements, suitability recommendations and health/longevity claims.
